questions.stem: The INTEGRATED GUIDED MISSILE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (IGMDP), started in 1983, was led by:

options.option_text: Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM — 'Missile Man of India'; developed PRITHVI, AGNI, AKASH, TRISHUL, NAG

questions.explanation: IGMDP (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme) — Indian ministry of defence's ambitious programme (1983-2008) to develop indigenous missiles. LAUNCHED 26 JULY 1983. Director: Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM (later 11th President of India, 2002-07; 'MISSILE MAN OF INDIA'). AIMED to end India's dependence on foreign arms; fund allocated ₹389 crore initially. 5 MISSILE PROJECTS: (1) PRITHVI — surface-to-surface TACTICAL ballistic; range 150-350 km; Army (Prithvi-I 150 km), Air Force (Prithvi-II 250 km), Navy (Prithvi-III / Dhanush 350 km). First tested 25 Feb 1988. (2) AGNI — long-range ballistic missile series (originally, a tech demonstrator; later separate IRBM programme). (3) TRISHUL — short-range surface-to-air; 9 km (tested but not productised). (4) AKASH — medium-range surface-to-air; 30 km; INDUCTED by Army + IAF; similar to US Patriot. (5) NAG — anti-tank guided missile; range 4-8 km; 'fire + forget'; mounted on Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA). PRINCIPAL DEVELOPER: DRDO (DEFENCE RESEARCH + DEVELOPMENT ORGANISATION) — India's premier military R&D body (est. 1958). DRDO has 50+ laboratories: DRDL (Hyderabad, missiles), BrahMos (JV with Russia), CRL Chandigarh, CVRDE Avadi (combat vehicles), LRDE (radars), RCI Hyderabad, ITR Chandipur (Interim Test Range — missile firing off Odisha coast). CURRENT DRDO CHAIRMAN: Dr. Samir V. Kamat (2023-). IGMDP officially CONCLUDED 8 Jan 2008 — succeeded by standalone missile programmes: AGNI (strategic ballistic, upgraded), BRAHMOS (supersonic cruise, Indo-Russian JV 2001; 290 km initially, 450-800 km now), NIRBHAY (subsonic cruise, 1,500 km), ASTRA (BVRAAM, air-to-air), QRSAM (Quick Reaction SAM), Helina (Helicopter-launched NAG). DR. KALAM's ROLE: served as DRDO chief, Scientific Adviser to Raksha Mantri, Secretary DRDO; led missile programme 1983-99; later headed POKHRAN-II nuclear tests (May 1998) as Principal Scientific Advisor. 11th PRESIDENT 2002-07; Bharat Ratna 1997; died 27 Jul 2015 in Shillong while giving lecture — aged 83.

questions.stem: India's LONGEST-range strategic ballistic missile, capable of hitting targets beyond 5000 km, is:

options.option_text: AGNI-V (ICBM-class, range 5,000-8,000+ km; MIRV-capable from 2024 Mission Divyastra); first launched 2012

questions.explanation: AGNI SERIES — India's indigenous medium to intercontinental-range ballistic missiles; strategic nuclear deterrent. (1) AGNI-I — SRBM, single-stage, range 700-1,200 km; inducted 2004. (2) AGNI-II — MRBM, 2-stage, range 2,000-3,000 km; inducted 2011. (3) AGNI-III — IRBM, 2-stage, range 3,000-5,500 km; inducted 2011. (4) AGNI-IV — IRBM, 2-stage, range 3,500-4,000 km; 1 tonne warhead. Inducted 2014. (5) AGNI-V — ICBM-class, 3-stage, range 5,000-8,000+ km (officially 5,000+; unofficial estimates up to 8,000 km); strategically can hit ALL of China + much of Europe. First tested 19 April 2012 from Wheeler Island (Abdul Kalam Island). Inducted into Strategic Forces Command (SFC) 2023. MIRV VARIANT — 'MISSION DIVYASTRA' — first test on 11 MARCH 2024 — successful test of MIRV (Multiple Independently-targetable Re-entry Vehicle) capability on Agni-V. India became 6th MIRV-capable nation (USA, Russia, China, UK, France + India). (6) AGNI-VI / K-5 / K-6 — in development; rumoured 8,000-12,000 km ICBM; SLBM variants. SUBMARINE-LAUNCHED BALLISTIC MISSILES (SLBM) — K series (named for Abdul Kalam): (a) K-15 / B-05 SAGARIKA — 750 km, deployed on INS Arihant nuclear submarine since 2018. (b) K-4 — 3,500 km, tested successfully, being deployed on Arihant-class SSBNs. (c) K-5, K-6 — future, 5,000-6,000 km. INS ARIHANT (commissioned 2016) = India's first ballistic missile submarine. INS Arighaat (2024), Aridhaman (future) — S4/S4* follow-on SSBNs. STRATEGIC TRIAD (land, air, sea-based nuclear delivery) — India achieved with Arihant-class + Agni-V. INDIA's NUCLEAR DOCTRINE: 'NO FIRST USE' (NFU) — credible minimum deterrent; massive retaliation to any nuclear attack; NO use against non-nuclear weapon states (except against states aligned with nuclear powers in aggression); civilian control via Political Council of Nuclear Command Authority (NCA). Estimated ~172 nuclear warheads (SIPRI 2024). India is NOT signatory to NPT or CTBT; maintained 'credible minimum deterrent' doctrine. NSG membership application pending (China blocking). Pokhran-I (Smiling Buddha, 18 May 1974) + Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti, 11 + 13 May 1998) = India's nuclear tests.

questions.stem: BRAHMOS, the world's FASTEST cruise missile, is a joint venture between INDIA + which country?

options.option_text: RUSSIA (NPO Mashinostroyenia); named after BRAHMAPUTRA + MOSKVA rivers; Mach 2.8-3.5; est. 1998, 1st test 2001

questions.explanation: BRAHMOS — supersonic CRUISE MISSILE; JOINT VENTURE between India's DRDO + Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia (NPOM). NAME: portmanteau of BRAHMAputra (India) + MOSkva (Russia). ESTABLISHED 1998 (JV signed by Dr. Kalam + Nikolai Mikhailov); company incorporated 2001. HEADQUARTERS: New Delhi (BrahMos Aerospace). FIRST TEST: 12 June 2001 from Chandipur (Odisha). SPECS: (1) SPEED — Mach 2.8 to 3.5 (nearly 3X speed of sound); world's FASTEST operational cruise missile. (2) RANGE — INITIAL 290 km (MTCR limit); EXTENDED to 450 km in 2017 after India joined MTCR (Missile Technology Control Regime) in 2016; 'BrahMos-ER' 500-800 km variant under development. (3) WARHEAD — 200-300 kg conventional (can carry nuclear but not a nuclear weapon system). (4) TWO-STAGE — solid booster + liquid-fuelled ramjet. (5) LENGTH 8.4m, diameter 0.6m. (6) LAUNCH PLATFORMS — LAND (Mobile Autonomous Launcher, 5-tube MAL), SHIP-launched (destroyers, frigates — INS Rajput first 2005; all new ships), SUBMARINE-launched (tested from INS Karanj), AIR-launched (integrated on Su-30MKI since 2016 — 'BrahMos-A' 2.5 tonne air variant; first live fire 2017). INDIA = FIRST country to have supersonic AIR-LAUNCHED CRUISE MISSILE. INDUCTED IN: (a) Indian Army (3 regiments + 4th under induction); (b) Indian Navy (30+ ships); (c) Indian Air Force (Su-30MKI squadron in Thanjavur). EXPORT: PHILIPPINES first export customer — signed Jan 2022, $375M deal for 3 batteries; delivery completed 2024. Other interested: Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, UAE. Also BrahMos-NG (Next Generation, smaller 1.5-tonne version, for Tejas LCA + MiG-29K + Rafale etc.) in development. BRAHMOS-II — HYPERSONIC (Mach 7-8), under development; JV with Russia. FAMOUSLY in March 2022, a BrahMos misfired from India (due to technical error, no warhead) and landed ~120km inside PAKISTAN (Mian Channu). Both countries handled it professionally; 3 IAF officers terminated. NO escalation. RAMJETS + SCRAMJETS: DRDO tested HSTDV (Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle) in 2020 + 2022 — indigenous scramjet at Mach 6+; foundation for BrahMos-II + Shaurya hypersonic programmes.

questions.stem: The CHIEF OF DEFENCE STAFF (CDS), created in 2019 as India's top uniformed officer, was FIRST held by:

options.option_text: General Bipin Rawat — 1 Jan 2020 – 8 Dec 2021; killed in Coonoor helicopter crash

questions.explanation: CHIEF OF DEFENCE STAFF (CDS) — newly-created POST (Dec 2019) of SENIOR-MOST uniformed officer of Indian Armed Forces. Recommended by KARGIL REVIEW COMMITTEE (K. Subrahmanyam) 1999, Naresh Chandra Task Force 2012; finally announced by PM Modi on 15 Aug 2019 Independence Day speech. CREATED via: (1) Amendments to Services Acts; (2) New 'Department of Military Affairs' (DMA) in Ministry of Defence — headed by CDS (ex-officio Secretary, DMA). ROLE: (1) SINGLE-POINT MILITARY advisor to Defence Minister (previously 3 service chiefs gave separate advice). (2) Promote 'JOINTNESS' — tri-services integration. (3) Permanent Chairman of CHIEFS OF STAFF COMMITTEE (COSC). (4) Not operational commander — each service chief retains operational command. (5) Oversees theaterisation — reorganising forces into integrated theatre commands. (6) Nuclear Command Authority advisor. CDS 1: GENERAL BIPIN RAWAT (27th COAS); assumed office 1 Jan 2020. Previously Chief of Army Staff (2017-19). TRAGICALLY DIED in MI-17V5 helicopter CRASH on 8 DECEMBER 2021 near Coonoor, Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu — he, wife Madhulika Rawat + 11 others perished; only 1 survivor (Gp Capt Varun Singh, who later died of burns Dec 15). Shock across nation. Enquiry by Tri-Services: pilot error in low-visibility (cloud + mountain); helicopter impacted hillside. VACANT CDS post from 8 Dec 2021 – 30 Sep 2022. CDS 2: GENERAL ANIL CHAUHAN (assumed 30 Sep 2022). Former GOC-in-C of Eastern Command; Kargil war veteran. Also: Air Chief Marshal + Navy Chief eligible; first two CDS have been Army. Term: 3 years; age 65 max. STRATEGIC DIRECTION: India is working towards THEATRE COMMANDS — integrating Army, Navy, AF in geographic commands (instead of service-wise). Proposed: Western Theatre (vs Pakistan), Northern Theatre (vs China), Maritime Theatre. Currently 17 single-service commands (7 Army + 7 Air + 3 Navy); ANDAMAN + NICOBAR COMMAND (ANC) = India's ONLY existing joint service theatre command since 2001; STRATEGIC FORCES COMMAND (SFC) — nuclear. CDS + DMA drive this reorganisation. Global examples: USA's 11 combatant commands, China's 5 theatre commands.

questions.stem: India conducted its FIRST nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha' (Pokhran-I), on:

options.option_text: 18 MAY 1974 — Pokhran, Rajasthan; declared 'peaceful nuclear explosion'; PM Indira Gandhi; yield ~8 kt

questions.explanation: INDIA's NUCLEAR TESTS — milestones: (1) POKHRAN-I / SMILING BUDDHA — 18 MAY 1974 (Buddha Purnima day, code named 'Smiling Buddha'). PM INDIRA GANDHI. Test at Pokhran, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Described as 'PEACEFUL NUCLEAR EXPLOSION' (PNE) to sidestep international obligations, though fuel was reactor-grade Plutonium. Yield ~8 kt (claimed; estimates 4-13 kt). Explosion went off in a 100m-deep shaft. Project led by BARC (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre) under Dr. RAJA RAMANNA (Project Director), with Dr. Homi Sethna (AEC Chairman), BASANTI DULAL NAG CHAUDHURI (ex-Scientific Adviser). INDIA's first PLUTONIUM used from CIRUS reactor (a Canadian-supplied heavy-water research reactor, contaminated with US heavy water). USA's + CANADA's reaction: sharp sanctions; end of civil nuclear cooperation; CANADA pulled out of NAPP; USA put India under strict tech sanctions. (2) POKHRAN-II / OPERATION SHAKTI — 11 + 13 MAY 1998. PM Atal Bihari VAJPAYEE; Principal Scientific Adviser Dr A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM coordinated; BARC director R. Chidambaram + DRDO + Atomic Energy Commission. 5 tests — 3 on 11 May 1998 + 2 on 13 May 1998. YIELDS: (a) 43 kt thermonuclear (hydrogen bomb) — disputed; some seismologists estimated 12-25 kt; Indian officials maintained 43 kt. (b) 12 kt fission. (c) 0.3 kt subkiloton. (d) 0.5 kt + 0.2 kt sub-kilotons on 13 May. Declared India as a NUCLEAR WEAPON STATE. SANCTIONS: UN + USA + G-7 imposed wide sanctions (mostly lifted by 2001). PAKISTAN's response: Chagai-I on 28 May 1998 (5 tests) + Chagai-II on 30 May (1 test) — bringing S. Asia into OVERT nuclear standoff. POST-1998: Subsequent elimination of sanctions with INDO-US CIVIL NUCLEAR DEAL 2005 (123 Agreement, Hyde Act); NSG waiver 2008; IAEA safeguards for civil reactors (2009). India now imports uranium (Kazakhstan, Russia, Canada) + civil nuclear cooperation with 14+ countries. 11 MAY = NATIONAL TECHNOLOGY DAY (declared 1999 by PM Vajpayee, commemorating Pokhran-II + AGNI + Hansa-3 aircraft tests). INDIA NEVER signed NPT (1968) or CTBT (1996). Follows 'NO FIRST USE' (NFU) nuclear doctrine + 'credible minimum deterrent'. STRATEGIC FORCES COMMAND (SFC, 2003) operates nuclear forces; POLITICAL COUNCIL of NCA (PM-led) has sole launch authority. Arsenal estimated ~170 warheads (SIPRI 2024).

questions.stem: INS VIKRANT, India's FIRST INDIGENOUS aircraft carrier, was commissioned on:

options.option_text: 2 SEPTEMBER 2022 — at Kochi; 45,000 tonnes; built by Cochin Shipyard Ltd; carries 30 aircraft (Mig-29K, Tejas, helos)

questions.explanation: INS VIKRANT (R11) — INDIA's FIRST INDIGENOUSLY BUILT AIRCRAFT CARRIER. Commissioned 2 SEPTEMBER 2022 by PM Narendra Modi at COCHIN SHIPYARD LIMITED (CSL), Kerala. BUILT by CSL (PSU). COST: ~₹20,000 CRORE. TIMELINE: keel laid 2009; launched 2013; undocked 2015; sea trials 2021; delivered July 2022; commissioned Sep 2022. SPECIFICATIONS: Displacement 45,000 tonnes; length 262m; beam 62m; draught 8.4m; speed 28 knots (52 km/h); range 7,500 nautical miles; crew 1,600 (including 160 officers). AIR WING: 30 aircraft — MiG-29K fighters (operational), Kamov Ka-31 AEW helicopters, MH-60R Romeo anti-submarine helicopters, HAL Dhruv/ALH, HAL Rudra. TEJAS MK-1A LCA + LCA-Navy being developed. Twin Island design. PROPULSION: 4 GE LM2500 gas turbines (88 MW total); 75% indigenous content (Navy target). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) INDIA became 6th country to design + build its own aircraft carrier (after US, UK, Russia, France, China). (2) Revives NAME 'VIKRANT' from India's first aircraft carrier (HMS Hercules → INS Vikrant, commissioned 1961, retired 1997) — which operated in 1971 Bangladesh War (sinking PNS Ghazi attempt to ambush it). HISTORIC INS VIKRANT now a MUSEUM SHIP — though plans scrapped; ship scrapped in 2014 (controversial; partial parts converted into memorials). ROYAL ENFIELD launched 'Classic 350 Vikrant' in 2023 using metal from original Vikrant. CURRENT INDIAN NAVY FLEET (2024-25): (1) 2 AIRCRAFT CARRIERS: INS Vikramaditya (ex-Soviet/Russian Admiral Gorshkov, commissioned 2013, 44,500t) + INS Vikrant (2022, 45,000t). (2) NUCLEAR SUBMARINES: INS Arihant (SSBN, 6,000t, commissioned 2016, K-15/K-4 SLBMs); INS Arighaat (2024); INS Chakra-III (SSN leased from Russia 2025, successor to Chakra-II returned 2021). (3) CONVENTIONAL SUBMARINES: 17 (Kalvari/Scorpene class 5, Shishumar/Type-209 4, Sindhughosh/Kilo 7). (4) DESTROYERS: 11 (Kolkata-class 3, Delhi-class 3, Visakhapatnam-class 4, Rajput-class 1). (5) FRIGATES: 15. (6) Total ~155 ships + 240 aircraft. IAC-II / INS VISHAL (proposed 3rd carrier, 65,000t, CATOBAR with EMALS catapults) under debate.

questions.stem: HAL TEJAS, India's indigenously-developed LIGHT COMBAT AIRCRAFT, is manufactured by:

options.option_text: HINDUSTAN AERONAUTICS LIMITED (HAL), Bengaluru — PSU under MoD; HAL is also India's primary helicopter + aero-engine manufacturer

questions.explanation: TEJAS — HAL LIGHT COMBAT AIRCRAFT (LCA); India's indigenously-developed 4.5-generation single-engine multirole fighter. DESIGNER: AERONAUTICAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (ADA, Bengaluru — under DRDO). MANUFACTURER: HINDUSTAN AERONAUTICS LIMITED (HAL) — PSU; India's premier aerospace company, HQ Bengaluru. PROGRAMME HISTORY: sanctioned 1983 (to replace ageing MiG-21); first flight Jan 2001; IOC (Initial Operational Clearance) 2011; FOC (Final Operational Clearance) 2019; series production began. VARIANTS: (1) Tejas Mk-1 — initial variant; 40 ordered (2005, 2010); currently in IAF service with 45 Sqn 'Flying Daggers' (Sulur TN) + 18 Sqn. (2) Tejas Mk-1A — upgraded; AESA radar (Uttam indigenous), SPJ (self-protection jammer), mid-air refueling probe, advanced weaponry (Astra, BrahMos-NG, BVRAAM); 83 ordered 2021 (Rs. 48,000 cr deal) + 97 more cleared 2023 — total 180 Mk-1A by 2028. (3) Tejas Mk-2 / MWF (Medium Weight Fighter) — bigger + more capable (17.5 tonnes MTOW, vs Mk-1's 13.5); Higher-thrust GE F414 engine; avionics + payload upgrade; first flight 2025-26; will replace MiG-29, Mirage 2000, Jaguar. 108 planned. (4) Tejas Navy — carrier variant for INS Vikrant (tested but pivoted to MiG-29K + future TEDBF — Twin Engine Deck-Based Fighter). ENGINE: currently GE F404-IN20; Mk-2 uses GE F414; 'KAVERI' engine (indigenous) still not fighter-grade ready after 40+ years. EXPORT: offered to MALAYSIA, ARGENTINA, EGYPT, PHILIPPINES, USA (test-bed), Indonesia. First export contract expected 2025-26. HAL OTHER PRODUCTS: (1) HAL DHRUV (advanced light helicopter, ~390 delivered); (2) HAL Rudra (Dhruv-WSI, attack variant); (3) HAL LCH Prachand (Light Combat Helicopter, FOC 2022); (4) HAL Chetak + Cheetah (licensed Aérospatiale); (5) HAL HTT-40 (basic trainer); (6) HAL IJT (intermediate jet trainer, troubled); (7) HAL Sukhoi Su-30MKI (licensed assembly, 272 in IAF); (8) HAL Hawk (licensed BAE AJT trainer); (9) HAL Dornier 228 (licensed utility). DEFENCE PSUs: (1) HAL — aero. (2) BEL (Bharat Electronics Ltd, Bengaluru) — electronics, radars. (3) BEML (Bharat Earth Movers, Bengaluru) — tanks, mining. (4) BDL (Bharat Dynamics, Hyderabad) — missiles. (5) MIDHANI (Mishra Dhatu Nigam, Hyderabad) — alloys. (6) GRSE (Garden Reach Shipbuilders, Kolkata). (7) MDL (Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Mumbai). (8) GSL (Goa Shipyard). (9) CSL (Cochin Shipyard). (10) HSL (Hindustan Shipyard, Vizag). OFB (Ordnance Factory Board) split into 7 DPSUs in 2021.

questions.stem: India became the 4TH COUNTRY to successfully demonstrate ANTI-SATELLITE (ASAT) capability with Mission Shakti on:

options.option_text: 27 MARCH 2019 — DRDO destroyed a target satellite in LEO (283 km) using indigenous ballistic missile; after USA, Russia, China

questions.explanation: MISSION SHAKTI — India's ANTI-SATELLITE (ASAT) weapon test. CONDUCTED 27 MARCH 2019 by DRDO from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island), Odisha. TARGET: Microsat-R (DRDO-launched in Jan 2019) — a 740 kg satellite in LOW EARTH ORBIT at 283 KM altitude. INTERCEPTOR: PDV (Prithvi Defence Vehicle) Mk-II — a kinetic kill vehicle based on Prithvi + Ashwin missile tech, part of India's BMD (Ballistic Missile Defence) programme. Hit target in ~3 MINUTES after launch in 'direct ascent' kinetic kill. OUTCOME: INDIA became 4th country (after USA 1959+2008, Russia/USSR 1968+2021, China 2007) to demonstrate ASAT. MOTIVATION: deter adversary's space assets (primarily China's; China's 2007 ASAT test shook India's strategic calculus). SPACE DEBRIS CONCERN: unlike China's 2007 test (at 865 km, created 3000+ long-lasting debris pieces), Mission Shakti chose LOW altitude (283 km) — most debris burned up in atmosphere within weeks to months; ISS + other high-orbit satellites unaffected. India announced test in advance to US Space Command. ~400 trackable debris pieces created, 24 crossing ISS altitude (fell within days). BY 2023, virtually all Mission Shakti debris decayed. POLITICAL: PM Modi announced the test to the nation via TV address 30 min after strike. Timing (just before 2019 general elections) was criticised by opposition as electioneering. Election Commission probe found no MCC violation. STRATEGIC: India established DEFENCE SPACE AGENCY (DSA, 2019) + DEFENCE SPACE RESEARCH ORGANISATION (DSRO) to build dedicated space assets for military. Joining a newer push by major space powers: (a) USA Space Force (2019, 6th military branch); (b) China PLA Strategic Support Force (2015, upgraded Aerospace Force 2024); (c) France Space Command (2019); (d) Russia Space Forces (2015). INDIA's NEXT: (a) MICROSAT-R-class ASATs; (b) Space-Situational Awareness (SSA) — Bengaluru centre + radars; (c) EMISAT, CartoSat-3, RISAT-2B — military ELINT/ SAR. SPACE DEFENCE TREATY: INDIA is party to OUTER SPACE TREATY 1967 (no WMDs in space); not to specific ASAT ban; global norms still being debated (UN COPUOS, Artemis Accords 2020 signed by India in 2023).

questions.stem: The RAFALE multirole fighter jets inducted by IAF (36 aircraft) are manufactured by:

options.option_text: DASSAULT AVIATION (France) — ordered 2016 at €7.87 billion; all 36 delivered by Dec 2022; Ambala + Hasimara bases

questions.explanation: RAFALE — 4.5-generation TWIN-ENGINE multirole omnirole fighter made by DASSAULT AVIATION, France. INDIA's INDUCTION: 36 RAFALE purchased via GOVERNMENT-TO-GOVERNMENT deal signed 23 September 2016 by Indian PM Modi + French President François Hollande at Paris. COST: €7.87 BILLION (~₹59,000 crore). Originally India's MMRCA tender (2007-2015) chose Rafale in 2012 for 126 fighters but deal collapsed over pricing + local manufacture (Transfer of Technology terms with HAL). Modi govt replaced with smaller 36-jet 'off-the-shelf' outright purchase. DELIVERY: all 36 delivered between July 2020 + Dec 2022. BASED at: 17 Squadron 'Golden Arrows' — Ambala (Haryana), 101 Squadron 'Falcons of Chamb + Akhnoor' — Hasimara (West Bengal, near Chinese border). SPECIFICATIONS: (1) Engines — 2× Snecma M88-4E (75 kN each afterburning). (2) Max speed Mach 1.8 (2,222 km/h). (3) Range: 3,700 km ferry. (4) Combat radius: 1,850 km with 3 drop tanks. (5) 14 weapon hardpoints. (6) AESA radar — Thales RBE2-AA. WEAPONS: Meteor BVRAAM (150+ km, beyond any Chinese/Pakistani BVRAAM), MICA IR + EM, SCALP-EG cruise missile (560 km), AM39 Exocet anti-ship, HAMMER PGM. Nuclear-capable. INDIA-specific modifications ('Rafale-DH' = with helmet-mounted sight, Israeli jammers, etc.). CONTROVERSY: 'RAFALE DEAL' became major political issue 2018-19; Congress accused price inflation + HAL being dropped as offset partner (Anil Ambani's Reliance Defence chosen). SC dismissed PIL in Dec 2018. CAG report (Feb 2019) found Modi-era deal 2.86% CHEAPER than UPA-era terms. NAVAL RAFALE ORDER: 26 Rafale-M (Marine) signed 28 April 2024 — for INS Vikrant, replacing MiG-29K; ₹63,887 crore. IAF FIGHTER INVENTORY (2025): Su-30MKI (272), Rafale (36, +plus naval), Mirage 2000 (45, upgrade by Thales), Jaguar (117, upgrade), MiG-29 (66), MiG-21 Bison (being retired), Tejas Mk-1/1A (40+180=220 total planned), Tejas Mk-2 future. FIFTH-GENERATION: AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft) — 5.5-gen stealth under development, first flight 2028-29, induction 2035+. S-400 TRIUMF air defence system: Russian, 5 squadrons ordered 2018 for $5.4 billion; 3 delivered by 2024, remaining 2 delayed by Ukraine war. Most potent long-range SAM in Indian arsenal.

questions.stem: The PARAM VIR CHAKRA (PVC), India's highest WARTIME gallantry award, was first awarded (posthumously) for the:

options.option_text: 1947-48 J&K War — Major Somnath Sharma, 4 Kumaon Regiment; KIA at Badgam defending Srinagar airfield on 3 Nov 1947

questions.explanation: PARAM VIR CHAKRA (PVC) — India's HIGHEST wartime military GALLANTRY AWARD. Instituted 26 January 1950; RETROSPECTIVE to 15 Aug 1947. DESIGNED BY Savitribai Khanolkar, an Indian-born Swiss woman. MEDAL: bronze, 3.5 cm diameter, with Ashok Chakra + 4 crossed swords in middle. INSCRIBED 'PARAM VIR CHAKRA' in Hindi + English. WORN on chest. RESERVED for 'MOST CONSPICUOUS ACT of BRAVERY or SELF-SACRIFICE' in presence of the enemy. FIRST RECIPIENT: MAJOR SOMNATH SHARMA, 4 Kumaon Regiment — KIA at BADGAM (near Srinagar Airport) on 3 NOVEMBER 1947 defending Srinagar airfield against Pakistani raiders during 1947-48 JK War. His last message: 'Enemy only 50 yards away. Heavily outnumbered. Devastating fire. WILL NOT WITHDRAW an inch BUT WILL FIGHT TO OUR LAST MAN + last ROUND'. His COURAGEOUS stand + that of his company delayed the raiders + saved Srinagar — without which J&K's fate could have been very different. His sister-in-law Savitribai Khanolkar designed the PVC medal; IRONIC that it was first awarded posthumously to her brother-in-law. GAZETTE: notified 21 June 1950. TOTAL AWARDED: 21 so far (since 1947). 14 POSTHUMOUS + 7 LIVING. RECIPIENTS (select): (1) Maj. Somnath Sharma (1947 JK). (2) Lance Naik Karam Singh (1947 JK). (3) Second Lt. Rama Raghoba Rane (1947 JK). (4) Havildar Major Piru Singh (1947 JK). (5) Naik Jadunath Singh (1947 JK). (6) Captain Gurbachan Singh Salaria (1961 Katanga UN Congo). (7) Major Dhan Singh Thapa (1962 Sino-Indian). (8) Subedar Joginder Singh (1962). (9) Major Shaitan Singh (1962). (10) Company Quartermaster Havildar Abdul Hamid (1965). (11) Lt. Col. Ardeshir Tarapore (1965). (12) Lance Naik Albert Ekka (1971). (13) Major Hoshiar Singh (1971). (14) Second Lt. Arun Khetarpal (1971 — AGE 21, posthumous). (15) Flying Officer Nirmaljit Singh Sekhon (1971 — ONLY IAF PVC). (16) Naib Subedar Bana Singh (1987 Siachen). (17) Major Ramaswamy Parameswaran (1987 Sri Lanka IPKF). (18) Captain Vikram Batra (1999 Kargil). (19) Captain Manoj Kumar Pandey (1999 Kargil). (20) Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav (1999 Kargil, LIVING). (21) Rifleman Sanjay Kumar (1999 Kargil, LIVING). KARGIL WAR (1999): 4 PVC awarded — largest cluster post-1971.
